items.answer: Payroll records belonging to a closed account are permanently erased 180 days after the closure date, unless a statutory retention hold has been registered against the account.

sources.title: Tessaline People Cloud - Retention settings for active accounts
sources.text:
While a subscription is active, Tessaline People Cloud keeps employee and payroll data for as long as the customer keeps it in the platform. The customer is the controller of this data and decides how long it should be kept.

Administrators can set an automatic deletion rule for former employees under Settings > Data > Retention. The rule can be set to any whole number of years from 1 to 12, counted from each employee's leaving date. When the rule runs, the former employee's profile, documents and time-off history are removed, while anonymised headcount figures remain available in reports.

For customers whose payroll is processed in Ireland, Tessaline retains payslip PDFs for 6 years after the end of the tax year to which they relate, even if a shorter deletion rule has been set, because local payroll rules require it. Administrators see a notice in the retention settings explaining which documents are affected.

Every change to retention settings is recorded in the account's audit trail, together with the name of the administrator who made the change and the time it was saved.

sources.title: Tessaline People Cloud - What happens to your data when you close your account
sources.text:
This article explains how Tessaline handles customer data after a People Cloud subscription ends, whether the customer cancels or the contract expires.

The account closure date is the last day of the final paid billing period. From that date, users can no longer sign in, and any scheduled payroll runs are cancelled.

Tessaline keeps a read-only export of the account's data available to the account owner for 30 days after the closure date. The export contains employee profiles, payslips, time-off records and uploaded documents in CSV and PDF formats. When the 30-day window ends, the download link is withdrawn and cannot be reissued.

Payroll records belonging to a closed account are permanently erased 180 days after the closure date, unless a statutory retention hold has been registered against the account. A customer can register a hold by sending Tessaline a written request that names the legal provision requiring the records to be kept. Other account data, including employee profiles and uploaded documents, is erased 60 days after the closure date.

Erasure covers Tessaline's production databases and file storage. Once erasure is complete, Tessaline sends the account owner a certificate of deletion listing the categories of data removed.

sources.title: Tessaline People Cloud - Support access to customer accounts
sources.text:
Tessaline support engineers do not have standing access to customer accounts. When a customer raises a ticket that requires an engineer to look at live data, the account owner must approve a support session from the Help menu.

Each support session lasts up to 8 hours and can be ended early by any administrator. During a session, the engineer can view payroll settings and employee records but cannot run payroll, change bank details or download documents. Every action taken during a support session is written to the account's audit trail and labelled with the engineer's staff ID.

Support sessions are not available once an account has been closed. Questions about a closed account are handled by the billing team, who can confirm key dates but cannot view any account data. Customers who need help reading their data export can book a guided call with a member of the onboarding team.

items.answer: Starting 3 March 2027, Mirefold will require hardware security key sign-in for all administrator accounts in Enterprise organisations.

sources.title: Mirefold Cloud - Setting up single sign-on
sources.text:
Single sign-on lets members of your organisation sign in to Mirefold Cloud through the identity provider your company already uses. SSO is available on the Business and Enterprise plans and works with most identity providers that offer SAML sign-in.

Before you can turn on SSO, you must verify ownership of your email domain by adding a TXT record to its DNS settings. Verification usually completes within an hour but can take up to 48 hours, depending on your DNS provider.

Once the domain is verified, enter your identity provider's sign-in address, entity ID and signing certificate on the Single sign-on page. We recommend testing with a single member before you enforce SSO for everyone. When SSO is enforced, members with an email address on the verified domain can no longer sign in with a Mirefold password.

Enterprise organisations can also connect automatic user provisioning, so that people added to or removed from groups in the identity provider are added to or removed from the Mirefold organisation within 40 minutes.

sources.title: Mirefold Cloud - Session and access key lifetimes
sources.text:
Console sessions end automatically after 12 hours, or after 2 hours without activity, whichever comes first. Organisation owners can shorten the inactivity limit to as little as 15 minutes under Organisation settings > Security, but cannot extend it beyond 2 hours.

Programmatic access keys do not expire by default. Owners can set a maximum key age of 30, 90 or 180 days; when a key reaches that age it stops working, and the person who created it receives an email asking them to rotate it. Mirefold recommends a maximum age of 90 days for keys used in production pipelines.

Access keys that have not been used for 400 days are disabled automatically on all plans. A disabled key can be re-enabled by an owner within 30 days, after which it is deleted and must be replaced.

All key creation, rotation and deletion events are shown in the organisation's activity log for 13 months.

sources.title: Mirefold Cloud - Security notice: hardware security keys for administrators
sources.text:
Mirefold is tightening sign-in requirements for administrators of Enterprise organisations on the Mirefold Cloud console. Administrator accounts can change billing settings, create access keys and delete entire projects, which makes them the most valuable target for credential phishing.

Starting 3 March 2027, Mirefold will require hardware security key sign-in for all administrator accounts in Enterprise organisations. From that date, one-time codes sent by text message and codes generated by authenticator apps will no longer be accepted as a second factor for those accounts.

To prepare, each affected administrator should register at least two security keys, so that losing one key does not lock them out of the console. Keys can be registered now under Account > Security > Sign-in methods. Organisation owners can see which administrators have not yet registered two keys on the Security Readiness page, which is refreshed every 24 hours.

If an administrator loses all of their registered keys after the deadline, another organisation owner must verify their identity and issue a single-use recovery link that expires after 12 hours. Organisations with only one owner should add a second owner before the deadline.

Mirefold will email reminders to organisation owners 60 days and 14 days before the security key requirement takes effect.

items.question: How long does Quenmoor keep driver-facing camera footage?
items.answer: Quenmoor deletes driver-facing camera footage recorded between 1 July 2026 and 31 December 2026 after 14 days.

sources.title: Quenmoor Fleet - Camera footage retention update
sources.text:
Quenmoor Fleet customers who use the DualView in-cab camera record two video streams: a road-facing stream that captures the view through the windscreen, and a driver-facing stream that captures the driver's seat. Footage is uploaded to Quenmoor's cloud only when a safety event is detected or a fleet manager requests a clip.

Following an agreement with the Drivers' Consultative Council, Quenmoor deletes driver-facing camera footage recorded between 1 July 2026 and 31 December 2026 after 14 days. Road-facing camera footage is unaffected by the agreement and is deleted after 45 days.

For footage recorded during the same period, fleet managers must enter a reason in the platform before they can open a driver-facing clip, and each viewing is listed in the driver's own activity history in the Quenmoor Driver app.

The Council will review the arrangement in November 2026, and Quenmoor will publish any changes that apply to footage recorded from 1 January 2027 onward. Customers do not need to change any settings; the deletion period is applied automatically to every fleet.

sources.title: Quenmoor Fleet - How safety events are detected
sources.text:
The DualView camera contains an accelerometer and a gyroscope that measure how the vehicle moves. Quenmoor treats a movement as a safety event when it crosses one of the thresholds below, which fleet managers can adjust on the Safety settings page.

Harsh braking: deceleration greater than 0.45 g for at least half a second.
Harsh acceleration: acceleration greater than 0.35 g for at least one second.
Sharp cornering: lateral force greater than 0.40 g.
Possible collision: any impact above 2.5 g.

When an event is detected, the camera saves a clip covering the 10 seconds before and the 10 seconds after the event and uploads it as soon as the vehicle has a mobile signal. Events normally appear on the fleet dashboard within 5 minutes. Drivers hear an in-cab chime for harsh braking and sharp cornering so that they can adjust straight away; no chime is played for possible collisions.

sources.title: Quenmoor Fleet - Location history
sources.text:
Quenmoor trackers record the vehicle's position every 30 seconds while the ignition is on, and every 30 minutes while the vehicle is parked. Positions are used to build trip records, show live vehicle locations on the map and calculate mileage for expense reports.

Raw position points are kept for 13 months. Trip summaries, which show the start and end address, distance and duration of each journey, are kept for 6 years so that fleets can meet tax and mileage record-keeping requirements.

Drivers of vehicles that are approved for personal use can switch on Private Mode from the Quenmoor Driver app outside their working hours. While Private Mode is on, the tracker records only the distance travelled, not the route or position. Fleet managers can see that Private Mode was used but cannot see where the vehicle went.

sources.title: Quenmoor Fleet - How safety events are detected
sources.text:
The DualView camera contains an accelerometer and a gyroscope that measure how the vehicle moves. Quenmoor treats a movement as a safety event when it crosses one of the thresholds below, which fleet managers can adjust on the Safety settings page.

Harsh braking: deceleration greater than 0.45 g for at least half a second.
Harsh acceleration: acceleration greater than 0.35 g for at least one second.
Sharp cornering: lateral force greater than 0.40 g.
Possible collision: any impact above 2.5 g.

sources.title: Kestrove Read - Privacy notice for schools: pupil voice recordings
sources.text:
Kestrove Read lets pupils record themselves reading a passage aloud so that their teacher can follow how their fluency develops over the year. This section of our privacy notice explains what happens to those recordings.

Recordings are stored in encrypted form in Kestrove's data centre in the United Kingdom. They are linked to the pupil's school account and are never connected to a personal email address or phone number.

Pupil recordings are sent to Kestrove's speech-scoring subprocessor, Arventa Labs, when the school has switched on automated fluency scoring. Arventa Labs uses each recording only to return a words-correct-per-minute score and a list of misread words to the teacher, and it must delete the audio within 72 hours of returning the score. Arventa Labs processes recordings in the United Kingdom and may not transfer them elsewhere.

Recordings held by Kestrove are deleted at the end of the school year in which they were made, unless the teacher has added them to the pupil's progress portfolio. Portfolio recordings are deleted when the pupil leaves the school or when the school's subscription ends, whichever happens first.

sources.title: Kestrove - Data processing terms for schools: summary
sources.text:
When a school uses Kestrove Read, the school is the controller of pupil data and Kestrove acts as its processor. Kestrove processes pupil data only on the school's documented instructions, which are set out in the order form and in the settings the school chooses in the admin console.

Kestrove staff who can access pupil data are bound by confidentiality obligations and complete safeguarding training every year. If Kestrove becomes aware of a personal data breach affecting pupil data, it will notify the school's nominated contact without undue delay and in any case within 48 hours.

Schools may audit Kestrove's compliance once per year by giving 30 days' written notice, or may instead rely on Kestrove's most recent independent security report. Kestrove will tell schools at least 30 days before it adds or replaces a subprocessor, and a school may object by contacting its account manager.

sources.title: Kestrove Read - Setting up classes and pupil accounts
sources.text:
Before pupils can use Kestrove Read, a school administrator needs to create classes and pupil accounts. Most schools do this by connecting Kestrove to their management information system, which copies across class lists each night. Schools without a connection can upload a spreadsheet containing each pupil's first name, last initial, year group and class.

Pupils do not need an email address. Instead, each pupil signs in by choosing their class and then picking their own picture password from a grid of nine images. Teachers can print sign-in cards for younger pupils and can reset a picture password from the class page at any time.

When a pupil moves class during the year, their reading history moves with them. When a pupil leaves the school, the administrator should archive their account so that it no longer counts towards the school's licence.

sources.title: Orrinvale Payments - Card-security compliance overview
sources.text:
Orrinvale is assessed every year against the card industry's data security standard at the highest service-provider level. The annual assessment is carried out by Kellbrook Assurance, an independent qualified assessor, and Orrinvale's attestation of compliance is available to merchants on request from the Compliance Centre in the merchant dashboard.

Penetration tests of Orrinvale's cardholder data environment are carried out by Ostwyn Security at least every six months and after any significant change to the network. Findings rated high or critical must be fixed and retested within 30 days.

Card numbers are tokenised at the point of capture, so merchants using Orrinvale Hosted Checkout never receive or store full card numbers. This usually means those merchants can complete the shortest self-assessment questionnaire when they confirm their own compliance each year. Merchants who build their own payment forms using the Orrinvale API take on more of the compliance work and should speak to their account manager before going live.

sources.title: Orrinvale Payments - Security incident notification commitments
sources.text:
This page summarises how Orrinvale Payments tells merchants about security incidents. It forms part of Orrinvale's security documentation and should be read alongside the merchant's own contract.

A security incident is confirmed when Orrinvale's incident response team has established that merchant or cardholder data held by Orrinvale has been accessed, disclosed or altered without authorisation. sources.title: Halvicor Mutual - How long we keep claims information
sources.text:
We keep the information connected with a claim for as long as we need it to handle the claim, deal with any complaint and meet our legal and regulatory obligations.

Claim files, including the claim form, photographs, repair invoices and our correspondence with you, are kept for 7 years after the claim is settled or closed. Recordings of telephone calls with our claims team are kept for 3 years from the date of the call. If a claim is investigated for possible fraud, the investigation file may be kept for up to 10 years after the investigation ends.

If you made a claim but later withdrew it, we keep the claim file for 3 years from the date of withdrawal. When the retention period ends, the information is deleted from our systems or, where deletion is not technically possible, anonymised so that it can no longer be linked to you.

sources.title: Halvicor Mutual - Recognising genuine messages from us
sources.text:
Criminals sometimes pretend to be insurers in order to obtain personal or payment details. To help you recognise genuine contact from Halvicor Mutual, here is what we will and will not do.

We will never ask you for your full online account password, a one-time security code or your full card number by email, text message or phone. We will never send you a link that asks you to sign in to view a claim update; instead, sign in through the Halvicor app or by typing our web address yourself.

Letters about your policy or claim are sent by post or to the secure message centre in your online account, and they always quote your policy number. If you receive a message that you are unsure about, do not reply to it. Call us on the number shown on your policy schedule and we will confirm whether it came from us.

sources.title: Halvicor Mutual - Notice of a data security incident affecting claim documents
sources.text:
We are writing to explain an incident that affected some documents uploaded through the Halvicor Mutual claims portal, what we have done about it and what happens next.

What happened. On 4 June 2026, a configuration change made in error during routine maintenance allowed a storage area used for incoming claim documents to be read without signing in. Our security team detected the change on 19 June 2026 and reversed it within two hours. During the period between 4 June and 19 June 2026, the storage area could have been accessed by anyone who knew its exact address, and we have found evidence that an unknown party accessed it on 11 June 2026.

What information was involved. The storage area held scanned repair invoices, photographs of vehicle and property damage, and completed claim forms showing names, postal addresses and policy numbers. It did not hold payment card or bank account details.

What we are doing. By 31 July 2026, Halvicor will write to every policyholder who uploaded a claim document between 4 June and 19 June 2026. Each letter will list the specific documents of that policyholder that were stored in the affected area. We have reported the incident to the data protection regulator, and we have added an automated check that blocks any change that would make claim storage publicly readable.

sources.title: Sablewick Chat - Message retention settings
sources.text:
By default, Sablewick Chat keeps every message and file for as long as the workspace exists. Workspace owners on the Business and Enterprise plans can set a retention period instead, after which messages and files are deleted automatically.

Retention periods can be set for the whole workspace or, on Enterprise, separately for public channels, private channels and direct messages. The shortest period available is 1 day and the longest is 10 years. When a message reaches the end of its retention period, it is removed from search results immediately and deleted from storage within 7 days.

Changes to retention settings apply to existing messages as well as new ones, so shortening a retention period can delete a large amount of history at once. Owners see a confirmation screen showing how many messages will be affected before the change is saved.

sources.title: Vantreth Health - How we protect your health information
sources.text:
The Vantreth symptom-tracking app stores the symptoms, medications and notes you record so that you can see patterns over time and share a summary with your clinician. We take the protection of this information seriously.

We rejected 8 requests as legally invalid or too broad, and the remaining 3 were withdrawn by the requesting agency.

In 2024 we received 9 requests and disclosed some data in response to 5 of them.

We notify affected users before disclosing their data unless a court order prohibits us from doing so. Where notice was delayed by a court order, we notify the user once the order expires. We never give any agency direct or bulk access to our systems, and we have not received any request for bulk data.

For your security, payments to new recipients are limited to 500 euros per day for the first 24 hours after a new phone is registered. Existing recipients and standing orders are not affected.

If you register a third phone, the phone you registered first is removed automatically and you will receive an email telling you which device was removed. If you did not make this change, call us straight away using the number on the back of your card.

sources.title: Wrenhollow - Contact us
sources.text:
The quickest way to reach us is through the chat button in the bottom corner of the Wrenhollow app. You can also email our support team from the Help page.

Our support team works from the Lisbon office, Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 18:00 Western European Time. The office is closed at weekends and on Portuguese public holidays, and chats or emails received while it is closed are answered on the next working day.

Customers on the Studio plan can also book a 30-minute call with a product specialist. Calls are available on Tuesdays and Thursdays and can be booked up to two weeks ahead.

If you have found a security vulnerability, please do not report it through chat. Use the security report form on our Trust page so that it reaches the right people.

sources.title: Wrenhollow - Two-step verification
sources.text:
Two-step verification adds a second check when you sign in to Wrenhollow, so that someone who learns your password still cannot get into your account. You can turn it on under Settings > Security.

Wrenhollow supports authenticator apps and hardware security keys. Text-message codes are not offered because they can be intercepted. When you turn on two-step verification, we give you ten single-use backup codes; store them somewhere safe, because they are the only way to sign in if you lose both your phone and your key.

Workspace administrators on the Studio plan can require two-step verification for every member. Members who have not set it up within 7 days of the requirement being switched on are signed out until they do.

sources.title: Wrenhollow - Privacy FAQ: exporting and deleting your data
sources.text:
Can I get a copy of my data?
Yes. Go to Settings > Privacy > Export to request an archive of your projects, comments and account details. Archives are generated automatically and the download link is emailed to you, usually within an hour.

Can I delete my account?
Yes. Go to Settings > Privacy > Delete account. Account deletions are carried out manually by our Trust Operations team after they have confirmed that the request came from the account owner and that the account has no unpaid invoices. Once a deletion has been carried out it cannot be undone, and we cannot recover any of your projects.

What happens to projects I share with others?
If you own a project that other people work on, you will be asked to transfer ownership before your account is deleted. Projects that are not transferred are deleted along with your account.

sources.title: Paceharbor Help Centre - How long is my route history kept?
sources.text:
Your route history is what lets you look back at where you ran, rode or walked. Paceharbor keeps your workout location history for 24 months. When a route reaches that age it is removed automatically, but the summary of the workout - distance, duration and date - stays in your training log.

If you want to keep a route for longer, you can export it as a GPX file from the workout's menu before it is removed. Exported files are stored on your own device and are not affected by the retention period.

Routes from workouts you have deleted are removed straight away and cannot be exported afterwards, so export anything you want to keep before deleting a workout. If you think a route has been removed by mistake, contact us from the Help menu and include the date of the workout.

sources.title: Paceharbor - Sharing workouts with followers
sources.text:
Every workout you record in Paceharbor has its own visibility setting: Only me, Followers or Everyone. New accounts start with Followers as the default, and you can change the default under Settings > Privacy.

Followers can see the workouts you share with them in their feed, together with your route map, distance, pace and any photos you add. They cannot see your heart-rate data unless you switch on Share health metrics for that workout.

If you set a workout to Everyone, it can appear on public leaderboards for the segments you completed. You can remove yourself from all leaderboards at once by turning off Leaderboard participation, which also hides your name on segment pages. People you remove from your followers are not notified.

Paceharbor collects precise location data from your phone while you are recording a workout, so that we can map your route and calculate distance, pace and elevation. We do not collect location data when no workout is being recorded.

Route maps are visible only to you unless you choose to share a workout with followers or make it public. You can hide the start and end of your routes by setting a privacy zone of 200, 500 or 1,000 metres around any address.

We retain workout location history for 12 months, after which route data is deleted and only the workout's total distance, duration and date are kept. standalone.question: Where does Arventa Labs process Kestrove Read recordings?
standalone.answer: Arventa Labs processes Kestrove Read pupil recordings in the United Kingdom [S2].

sources.title: Kestrove Read - Privacy notice for schools: pupil voice recordings
sources.text:
Kestrove Read lets pupils record themselves reading a passage aloud so that their teacher can follow how their fluency develops over the year. This section of our privacy notice explains what happens to those recordings.

Recordings are stored in encrypted form in Kestrove's data centre in the United Kingdom. They are linked to the pupil's school account and are never connected to a personal email address or phone number.

Pupil recordings are sent to Kestrove's speech-scoring subprocessor, Arventa Labs, when the school has switched on automated fluency scoring. Arventa Labs uses each recording only to return a words-correct-per-minute score and a list of misread words to the teacher, and it must delete the audio within 72 hours of returning the score. Arventa Labs processes recordings in the United Kingdom and may not transfer them elsewhere.

Recordings held by Kestrove are deleted at the end of the school year in which they were made, unless the teacher has added them to the pupil's progress portfolio. Portfolio recordings are deleted when the pupil leaves the school or when the school's subscription ends, whichever happens first.

sources.title: Kestrove - Data processing terms for schools: summary
sources.text:
When a school uses Kestrove Read, the school is the controller of pupil data and Kestrove acts as its processor. Kestrove processes pupil data only on the school's documented instructions, which are set out in the order form and in the settings the school chooses in the admin console.

Kestrove staff who can access pupil data are bound by confidentiality obligations and complete safeguarding training every year. If Kestrove becomes aware of a personal data breach affecting pupil data, it will notify the school's nominated contact without undue delay and in any case within 48 hours.

Schools may audit Kestrove's compliance once per year by giving 30 days' written notice, or may instead rely on Kestrove's most recent independent security report. Kestrove will tell schools at least 30 days before it adds or replaces a subprocessor, and a school may object by contacting its account manager.

sources.title: Kestrove Read - Setting up classes and pupil accounts
sources.text:
Before pupils can use Kestrove Read, a school administrator needs to create classes and pupil accounts. Most schools do this by connecting Kestrove to their management information system, which copies across class lists each night. Schools without a connection can upload a spreadsheet containing each pupil's first name, last initial, year group and class.

Pupils do not need an email address. Instead, each pupil signs in by choosing their class and then picking their own picture password from a grid of nine images. Teachers can print sign-in cards for younger pupils and can reset a picture password from the class page at any time.

When a pupil moves class during the year, their reading history moves with them. When a pupil leaves the school, the administrator should archive their account so that it no longer counts towards the school's licence.

sources.title: Callowmere Energy - Annual privacy report 2025 (extract)
sources.text:
In 2025 Callowmere Energy received 1,240 requests from customers exercising their data protection rights. Of these, 815 were requests for a copy of personal data, and the rest were requests for deletion or correction of personal data. We completed 97% of all requests within the one-month deadline. The remaining requests were completed within an extended deadline after we had told the customer why more time was needed.

The most common reason for an extension was that a request covered smart meter readings held by our metering partner, which we have to retrieve separately. We have since agreed a faster retrieval process with the partner, which took effect in January 2026.

We received 6 complaints about our handling of personal data, all of which were resolved without the regulator becoming involved. We reported 2 personal data breaches to the regulator in 2025, and neither involved financial information.

sources.title: Callowmere Energy - Smart meter data: what we collect and why
sources.text:
If you have a smart meter, it can send us readings of how much gas and electricity you use. By default, Callowmere collects one reading per day, which we use to send you accurate bills instead of estimates.

You can choose to share half-hourly readings instead. These let us offer time-of-use tariffs and show you a breakdown of when you use the most energy. We only collect half-hourly readings with your consent, and you can withdraw it at any time in the Callowmere app.

You can also opt out of daily readings and share only one reading a month, which is the minimum we need for billing. Readings are transmitted over the metering partner's secure network and are never used for marketing unless you have separately agreed to receive offers based on your usage.

gold.target_claim: Deletion requests were about 34% of the 1,240 data protection requests Callowmere Energy received in 2025.

gold_spans.quote: In 2025 Callowmere Energy received 1,240 requests from customers exercising their data protection rights.
Of these, 815 were requests for a copy of personal data, and the rest were requests for deletion or correction of personal data.

construction.note: 34% equals 425/1,240, which treats every non-access request as a deletion; S1 only gives the combined deletion-or-correction count, so the number of deletion requests is a missing input.

standalone.question: If I uninstall the Nimbrel Drive desktop app, are my files removed from Nimbrel's servers?
standalone.answer: Uninstalling the Nimbrel Drive desktop client removes your files from Nimbrel's servers.

sources.title: Nimbrel Drive - Storage plans
sources.text:
Every Nimbrel Drive account includes 15 GB of storage, shared between your files, the trash and your file version history. If you need more space, you can upgrade to Nimbrel Drive Plus with 1 TB, or to Nimbrel Drive Family with 2 TB that can be shared by up to five people.

When you reach your storage limit, existing files stay available, but new files will not upload or sync until you free up space or upgrade. We will email you when you reach 90% of your limit and again when you reach 100%.

If you downgrade to a smaller plan while using more storage than it includes, your files are not deleted. You will still be able to view and download them, but you will not be able to add new files until you are back under the limit.

sources.title: Nimbrel Drive - Using the desktop sync client
sources.text:
The Nimbrel Drive desktop client keeps a folder on your computer in step with the files stored in your Nimbrel Drive cloud account. Changes you make in the folder are uploaded automatically, and changes made elsewhere are downloaded to your computer.

Some customers expect that uninstalling or pausing the desktop client will remove their files from Nimbrel's servers; however, files remain stored in your Nimbrel Drive cloud account until you delete them in the web app. Pausing sync simply stops changes from being uploaded or downloaded until you resume it, and uninstalling the client leaves the local copies of your files on your computer.

If you want to remove files from Nimbrel's servers, delete them in the web app and then empty the trash. Files deleted from the synced folder on your computer are also moved to the trash in the web app, where they stay for 30 days before they are permanently deleted.

gold.target_claim: Uninstalling the Nimbrel Drive desktop client removes the user's files from Nimbrel's servers.

gold_spans.quote: Some customers expect that uninstalling or pausing the desktop client will remove their files from Nimbrel's servers; however, files remain stored in your Nimbrel Drive cloud account until you delete them in the web app.

planted_change.from: files remain stored in your Nimbrel Drive cloud account
planted_change.to: removes your files from Nimbrel's servers

construction.note: The fragment 'uninstalling ... will remove their files from Nimbrel's servers' seems to support the claim, but the same sentence negates it ('however, files remain stored'), so the context negates and the label is contradicted/negation.

standalone.question: Who carries out Orrinvale's annual card-security assessment?
standalone.answer: Ostwyn Security carries out Orrinvale's annual card-security assessment.

sources.title: Orrinvale Payments - Card-security compliance overview
sources.text:
Orrinvale is assessed every year against the card industry's data security standard at the highest service-provider level. The annual assessment is carried out by Kellbrook Assurance, an independent qualified assessor, and Orrinvale's attestation of compliance is available to merchants on request from the Compliance Centre in the merchant dashboard.

Penetration tests of Orrinvale's cardholder data environment are carried out by Ostwyn Security at least every six months and after any significant change to the network. Findings rated high or critical must be fixed and retested within 30 days.

Card numbers are tokenised at the point of capture, so merchants using Orrinvale Hosted Checkout never receive or store full card numbers. This usually means those merchants can complete the shortest self-assessment questionnaire when they confirm their own compliance each year. Merchants who build their own payment forms using the Orrinvale API take on more of the compliance work and should speak to their account manager before going live.

sources.title: Orrinvale Payments - Security incident notification commitments
sources.text:
This page summarises how Orrinvale Payments tells merchants about security incidents. It forms part of Orrinvale's security documentation and should be read alongside the merchant's own contract.

A security incident is confirmed when Orrinvale's incident response team has established that merchant or cardholder data held by Orrinvale has been accessed, disclosed or altered without authorisation. Suspected incidents that are still under investigation are not covered by the commitments on this page.

For merchants on an Orrinvale Enterprise contract, Orrinvale will notify the merchant of a confirmed security incident affecting their data within 24 hours. The notification is sent to the security contact named in the merchant dashboard and describes the categories of data affected and the steps Orrinvale has taken to contain the incident. Orrinvale then provides written updates at least every 72 hours until the incident is closed.

Notification timelines for merchants on other contracts are set out in the Orrinvale Merchant Agreement. Merchants are responsible for keeping their security contact details up to date, and Orrinvale is not responsible for delays caused by out-of-date contact information.

sources.title: Orrinvale Payments - Vulnerability disclosure programme
sources.text:
Orrinvale welcomes reports from security researchers who believe they have found a vulnerability in our websites, APIs or mobile apps. Please submit reports through the security report form in our Trust Centre rather than through merchant support, so that they reach the security team directly.

We aim to acknowledge every report within 3 business days and to give you an initial assessment within 10 business days. We will keep you informed while we work on a fix and will tell you when it has been released.

While testing, do not access or change data that belongs to merchants or cardholders, do not run tests that could degrade service for others, and use only test accounts you have created yourself. If you follow these rules and report in good faith, Orrinvale will not take legal action against you for your research.

Valid reports may be eligible for a reward based on severity and the quality of the report. Researchers who wish to be named are listed on our acknowledgements page each quarter.

gold.target_claim: Ostwyn Security performs Orrinvale's annual card-security assessment.

Penetration tests of Orrinvale's cardholder data environment are carried out by Ostwyn Security at least every six months

construction.note: Reuses the s7-f5 passages. S1 names Kellbrook Assurance as the annual assessor and gives Ostwyn Security a different role (penetration testing), so attributing the assessment to Ostwyn is contradicted.

standalone.question: When did Halvicor detect the claims storage misconfiguration?
standalone.answer: Halvicor's security team detected the claim storage misconfiguration on 4 June 2026.

sources.title: Halvicor Mutual - How long we keep claims information
sources.text:
We keep the information connected with a claim for as long as we need it to handle the claim, deal with any complaint and meet our legal and regulatory obligations.

Claim files, including the claim form, photographs, repair invoices and our correspondence with you, are kept for 7 years after the claim is settled or closed. Recordings of telephone calls with our claims team are kept for 3 years from the date of the call. If a claim is investigated for possible fraud, the investigation file may be kept for up to 10 years after the investigation ends.

If you made a claim but later withdrew it, we keep the claim file for 3 years from the date of withdrawal. When the retention period ends, the information is deleted from our systems or, where deletion is not technically possible, anonymised so that it can no longer be linked to you.

sources.title: Halvicor Mutual - Recognising genuine messages from us
sources.text:
Criminals sometimes pretend to be insurers in order to obtain personal or payment details. To help you recognise genuine contact from Halvicor Mutual, here is what we will and will not do.

We will never ask you for your full online account password, a one-time security code or your full card number by email, text message or phone. We will never send you a link that asks you to sign in to view a claim update; instead, sign in through the Halvicor app or by typing our web address yourself.

Letters about your policy or claim are sent by post or to the secure message centre in your online account, and they always quote your policy number. If you receive a message that you are unsure about, do not reply to it. Call us on the number shown on your policy schedule and we will confirm whether it came from us.

sources.title: Halvicor Mutual - Notice of a data security incident affecting claim documents
sources.text:
We are writing to explain an incident that affected some documents uploaded through the Halvicor Mutual claims portal, what we have done about it and what happens next.

What happened. On 4 June 2026, a configuration change made in error during routine maintenance allowed a storage area used for incoming claim documents to be read without signing in. Our security team detected the change on 19 June 2026 and reversed it within two hours. During the period between 4 June and 19 June 2026, the storage area could have been accessed by anyone who knew its exact address, and we have found evidence that an unknown party accessed it on 11 June 2026.

What information was involved. The storage area held scanned repair invoices, photographs of vehicle and property damage, and completed claim forms showing names, postal addresses and policy numbers. It did not hold payment card or bank account details.

What we are doing. By 31 July 2026, Halvicor will write to every policyholder who uploaded a claim document between 4 June and 19 June 2026. Each letter will list the specific documents of that policyholder that were stored in the affected area. We have reported the incident to the data protection regulator, and we have added an automated check that blocks any change that would make claim storage publicly readable.

gold.target_claim: Halvicor's security team detected the claim storage misconfiguration on 4 June 2026.

gold_spans.quote: Our security team detected the change on 19 June 2026 and reversed it within two hours.

construction.note: Reuses the s7-f6 passages. 4 June 2026 is when the faulty change was made; S3 states detection happened on 19 June 2026, so the detection date is contradicted.

standalone.question: How long does Tessaline keep payslips for customers whose payroll runs in the Netherlands?
standalone.answer: For customers whose payroll is processed in the Netherlands, Tessaline retains payslip PDFs for 6 years after the end of the tax year to which they relate.

sources.title: Tessaline People Cloud - Retention settings for active accounts
sources.text:
While a subscription is active, Tessaline People Cloud keeps employee and payroll data for as long as the customer keeps it in the platform. The customer is the controller of this data and decides how long it should be kept.

Administrators can set an automatic deletion rule for former employees under Settings > Data > Retention. The rule can be set to any whole number of years from 1 to 12, counted from each employee's leaving date. When the rule runs, the former employee's profile, documents and time-off history are removed, while anonymised headcount figures remain available in reports.

For customers whose payroll is processed in Ireland, Tessaline retains payslip PDFs for 6 years after the end of the tax year to which they relate, even if a shorter deletion rule has been set, because local payroll rules require it. Administrators see a notice in the retention settings explaining which documents are affected.

Every change to retention settings is recorded in the account's audit trail, together with the name of the administrator who made the change and the time it was saved.

sources.title: Tessaline People Cloud - What happens to your data when you close your account
sources.text:
This article explains how Tessaline handles customer data after a People Cloud subscription ends, whether the customer cancels or the contract expires.

The account closure date is the last day of the final paid billing period. From that date, users can no longer sign in, and any scheduled payroll runs are cancelled.

Tessaline keeps a read-only export of the account's data available to the account owner for 30 days after the closure date. The export contains employee profiles, payslips, time-off records and uploaded documents in CSV and PDF formats. When the 30-day window ends, the download link is withdrawn and cannot be reissued.

Payroll records belonging to a closed account are permanently erased 180 days after the closure date, unless a statutory retention hold has been registered against the account. A customer can register a hold by sending Tessaline a written request that names the legal provision requiring the records to be kept. Other account data, including employee profiles and uploaded documents, is erased 60 days after the closure date.

Erasure covers Tessaline's production databases and file storage. Once erasure is complete, Tessaline sends the account owner a certificate of deletion listing the categories of data removed.

sources.title: Tessaline People Cloud - Support access to customer accounts
sources.text:
Tessaline support engineers do not have standing access to customer accounts. When a customer raises a ticket that requires an engineer to look at live data, the account owner must approve a support session from the Help menu.

Each support session lasts up to 8 hours and can be ended early by any administrator. During a session, the engineer can view payroll settings and employee records but cannot run payroll, change bank details or download documents. Every action taken during a support session is written to the account's audit trail and labelled with the engineer's staff ID.

Support sessions are not available once an account has been closed. Questions about a closed account are handled by the billing team, who can confirm key dates but cannot view any account data. Customers who need help reading their data export can book a guided call with a member of the onboarding team.

gold.target_claim: Tessaline retains payslip PDFs for 6 years after the relevant tax year for customers whose payroll is processed in the Netherlands.

gold_spans.quote: For customers whose payroll is processed in Ireland, Tessaline retains payslip PDFs for 6 years after the end of the tax year to which they relate

construction.note: Reuses the s7-f1 passages. The 6-year payslip rule is stated only for payroll processed in Ireland; no passage covers the Netherlands or excludes it, so the claim is unsupported.
